subject: AWS Marketplace private purchase path & buyer-approval tiers for HealthGrid
messages:
From: Emily Park <emily.park@healthgrid.com>
To: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.ai>
Cc: procurement@healthgrid.com
Date: Tue, 12 May 2026 09:15:00 -0700
Subject: Quick: Marketplace buying path + approval gates for our AWS PO

Hi Naomi,

Thanks for the demo last week. Procurement asked for a concrete purchase path for buying via AWS Marketplace (we want a private purchase rather than a SaaS invoice). Two things they need clarified before I escalate to finance: 1) recommended term length options you support in Private Offers (we require a preferred 12-mo but will consider 36-mo for deeper discounts), and 2) whether the buyer needs to route approvals through their marketplace buyer account or if we can accept purchase orders outside of the Marketplace flow and still be eligible for co-sell/ISV benefits.

I attached a short summary of our RFP. Can you send a recommended cadence: term/discount bands and the approvals path we should expect on the buyer side so I can include it in the packet to procurement?

Best,
Emily
Emily Park
Head of Cloud Procurement | HealthGrid
procurement@healthgrid.com

From: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.ai>
To: Emily Park <emily.park@healthgrid.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 12 May 2026 12:31:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Quick: Marketplace buying path + approval gates for our AWS PO

Hi Emily — thanks for the RFP summary, that helps. High level answers up front, then Ill loop in pricing/legal details:

- Term options: We support 1, 12, 24, and 36 month private offers. Typical enterprise is 12 or 36 months.
- Discount bands: For Marketplace private offers we often pair a commitment tier with % discount off list; see the attached pricing spreadsheet for exemplar tiers.
- Buyer approvals: To get Marketplace private offer procurement through the Marketplace (and preserve co-sell eligibility), the buyer should accept the private offer from within their AWS Marketplace customer account. If they purchase outside Marketplace (PO to vendor), they will not be recorded as a Marketplace transaction and that can affect AWS co-sell reporting.

Quick ask: can you confirm HealthGrids procurement org is able to accept an AWS private offer in their Marketplace console? If not, we have a secondary path (work with finance + co-sell team to evidence spend), but it requires extra doc and can delay co-sell credits.

I attached a sample pricing tier. Ben/Marcus: can you confirm the discount curve and whether a 36-mo commitment can trigger an additional promo credit for co-sell reporting?

Thanks,
Naomi
Naomi Feldman
Director, Strategic Accounts | Redwood Inference
naomi.feldman@redwood.ai

Attachment: redwood-pricing-tier-v2.xlsx (xlsx)
From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
To: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.ai>, Emily Park <emily.park@healthgrid.com>
Cc: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 13 May 2026 09:10:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Quick: Marketplace buying path + approval gates for our AWS PO

Thanks Naomi. Quick pricing notes:

- Core bands in spreadsheet: 0-25k, 25-150k, 150k-500k, 500k+. The % off list increases at each band; the 36mo flat-commit can be considered for an additional 5% on top of the band depending on expected ARR.
- We recommend structuring the PO as a committed spend per year (annualized for multi-year). For a 36mo, we typically show year-one discounted invoice and then T&Cs for the following years.

For HealthGrid: if theyre comfortable with 12mo we can move quickly with standard discounts; if they want 36mo well need an approval from GTM finance for the extra promo. Marcus: can you flag for the co-sell team if HealthGrid confirms marketplace acceptance? That preserves AWS reporting.

Ben
Ben Carter
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference
From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai>
To: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Emily Park <emily.park@healthgrid.com>
Date: Wed, 13 May 2026 10:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Quick: Marketplace buying path + approval gates for our AWS PO

Emily / Team — a couple of legal/term points to note from Marketplace side:

- Private Offer term lengths: AWS allows the seller to set the contract term; we must ensure our private offer SOW in DocuSign maps to the selected term.
- PO vs Marketplace acceptance: If HealthGrid requires a PO-first process, we can accept a PO, but to maintain Marketplace attribution we need the buyer to accept the Private Offer inside their account after we issue it. Procurement can sign the PO for internal purposes, then accept the Private Offer in console — thats the easiest path.
- Data residency / audit log ask: if HealthGrid needs longer retention or audit logs, flag that now so we can add a schedule to the SOW.

Ive drafted a short clause for the SOW about marketplace acceptance and co-sell attribution; I can drop it into the DocuSign once Emily confirms the desired term and whether they will accept the Private Offer in console.

- Vanessa Ortiz
Head of Legal Ops | Redwood Inference
From: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>
To: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Emily Park <emily.park@healthgrid.com>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 14 May 2026 11:45:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Quick: Marketplace buying path + approval gates for our AWS PO

Emily — quick co-sell note from my side: if HealthGrid accepts the private offer in their Marketplace console we can submit the opportunity for AWS co-sell within 48 hours of acceptance. That triggers co-sell enablement (listing the deal, routing to an AWS field rep). If they accept outside Marketplace only, we can still pursue joint motion but AWS attribution credits are harder and often delayed.

Operational ask for Naomi/Ben: once HealthGrid confirms term length, please provide expected ARR band so I can pre-register the opportunity with AWS and request co-sell resources. If they go 36mo, we should ask for a short joint announcement window and co-marketing assets.

Marcus
Marcus Lin
Head of GTM Partnerships | Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Quick: Marketplace buying path + approval gates for our AWS PO

Thanks all — quick answers from procurement:

- HealthGrid can accept a private offer in the AWS Marketplace console; that will be the preferred flow.
- Preferred initial term: 12 months. Procurement is open to 36 months but needs an explicit multi-year discount line item and finance sign-off.
- Expected ARR band estimate: $220k ARR (first 12 months).

Ill accept the private offer in-console once you issue it and will loop finance on the 36mo scenario. Please issue a 12mo private offer with the standard 25-150k band discount and a note that 36mo is eligible for additional discounts pending GTM finance review.

Emily
